pageCache.pageTitle: Meet Principal Marcus Huntley | Charter School Bermondsey
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Charter Bermondsey
Principal's Welcome
The Charter School Bermondsey was built with a simple but powerful belief: that every child thrives when they feel they truly belong, when they're supported to believe in themselves, and when they're challenged to become the very best version of who they can be.
We pride ourselves on being a school for families where children are genuinely known, genuinely challenged, and genuinely prepared for whatever comes next.
In a relatively short time, we've become a trusted choice for local families - known for strong academic teaching, a rich programme of creative, sporting and community opportunities, and the kind of pastoral care that's only possible when a school genuinely knows every student.
We're part of the Charter Schools Educational Trust, which means our students benefit from outstanding resources, exceptional teaching, and a clear pathway to two Outstanding Sixth Forms. But what makes Charter Bermondsey distinctive is something harder to measure — it's the relationships, the ambition, and the culture we build together every day.
I'd love for you to come and see it for yourself.
Marcus Huntley MA, NPQH — Principal

pageCache.pageTitle: French at the Charter School Bermondsey
pageCache.text:
French
Through learning French, students become confident, global citizens prepared for a multicultural world. With strong communication skills, they are ready to embrace new opportunities and cultures.
Curriculum Intent
Learning French opens doors to global cultures, helping students belong to an inclusive classroom where taking linguistic risks is welcomed with kindness. As Brené Brown notes, "True belonging only happens when we present our authentic, imperfect selves". We nurture the belief that speaking another language opens hearts—recalling Nelson Mandela's insight that speaking to someone in their language "goes to their heart". With integrity and curiosity, students adopt a scholarly routine of vocabulary mastery and grammar application. By exploring French-speaking cultures with high aspirations, students become fluent, open-minded linguists possessing "a second soul".
Key Stage 3
Taught in 2 x 55-minute lessons per week, our KS3 students focus on listening, speaking, reading, and writing. They are encouraged to speak with confidence and spontaneity, and to read and respond to a variety of texts in French.
Key Stage 4
With 3 x 55-minute lessons per week, KS4 students follow the AQA GCSE specification, developing their ability to communicate confidently with native speakers. They engage with authentic spoken and written material, deepening their understanding of the cultures where French is spoken. Enrichment opportunities, including trips and visits, help bring the language to life.
Explore more

pageCache.pageTitle: Drama at the Charter School Bermondsey
pageCache.text:
Drama
Our drama curriculum empowers you to express ideas, engage with diverse perspectives, and excel as a thoughtful performer and critic.
Curriculum Intent
In Drama, students belong to a safe creative community where mutual respect, kindness, and integrity underpin every class, rehearsal performance and reflection. We inspire students to believe in their creative potential, using a curious mind to interrogate diverse texts and human experiences. Adopting a scholarly approach to theatrical conventions and exploring new forms of artistic expression, students set high aspirations to become confident, articulate performers and insightful critics.
Key Stage 3
Taught through 1 x 55-minute period each week, students encounter a blend of theatre traditions and genres, including Greek Myth, Comedy, Shakespeare, Naturalism, and Epic Theatre. Our approach integrates English and History, enriching their emotional, academic, and creative development. For instance, students explore the lives of Victorian children and Greek Myth at the start of Year 7. As theatre makers, they create devised work and study scripts, developing their critical and objective writing skills.
Key Stage 4
In Key Stage 4, taught through 3 x 55-minute periods each week, students continue their journey as theatre makers and critics, working with theatre professionals to stage practical components of the AQA GCSE course. They focus on devising theatre, performing, and writing about plays and performances. The devising unit allows students to focus on various elements such as acting, costume, lighting, sound, or set design as they create their unique responses to prescribed stimuli. They explore the techniques of theatre practitioners such as Stanislavski, Brecht, and Mitchell, and gain firsthand experience by attending live performances.
Explore more

pageCache.pageTitle: Music at the Charter School Bermondsey
pageCache.text:
Music
Experience the joy of music while mastering essential skills. Our curriculum fosters creativity, builds confidence, and equips you with the tools to express your unique voice through diverse genres.
Curriculum Intent
In Music, students belong to a creative ensemble where sharing performance space requires kindness, respect, and mutual support. We instil the belief that every student can express themselves with integrity through dedication and practice. Fuelled by curiosity about global styles, students adopt a scholarly understanding of notation, theory, and composition. By exploring their musical talents with high aspirations, students become expressive, talented musicians who waltz through life with confidence.
Key Stage 3
Taught through 1 x 55-minute period each week, students are introduced to music from different times and cultures, developing their ability to use musical terminology appropriately. They have ample opportunities to compose and perform their own work based on various influences, enhancing their competence as both creators and performers.
Key Stage 4

pageCache.pageTitle: Citizenship at the Charter School Bermondsey
pageCache.text:
Citizenship
Empowering students to engage actively and thoughtfully in society.
Curriculum Intent
Citizenship exposes students to the legal, political, and social issues shaping modern Britain. The curriculum ensures students belong to a democratic society where they act with integrity and kindness toward others. We teach students to believe in the power of their voice, encouraging them to be curious about government systems and critical of societal issues. By exploring political arguments and adopting a scholarly approach to evidence and debate, students develop high aspirations to become active, informed citizens ready to shape their world.
Key Stage 3
Citizenship is taught through our personal development lesson, one 55-minute period each fortnight shared with PSHE and RSE. Please refer to the Personal Development on the curriculum page.
Assessment is ongoing and informal, including book marking, whole-class feedback and peer-to-peer feedback. In Years 7 to 9, students are formally assessed in November, March and June, using a combination of tests under examination conditions and work completed in class and for homework.
Key Stage 4
For those choosing Citizenship as an option, the course is taught through three 55-minute lessons per week. Assessment follows a similar pattern to Key Stage 3, with two major assessments in January and June using GCSE-style papers, alongside mock exams in November and March. Final GCSE examinations take place between May and June.
The core Citizenship curriculum is integrated with Religious Education, with informal assessment continuing in Years 10 and 11.
For questions about the Relating curriculum, please contact Jack Ward, Head of Religious Studies and Citizenship.
Explore more

Personal Development

pageCache.pageTitle: Computing at the Charter School Bermondsey
pageCache.text:
Computing
Empowering students to think critically and create confidently in a digital world. Together, we cultivate skills that will shape their futures.
Curriculum Intent
In Computing, we build a safe digital community where every student belongs through digital citizenship, collaboration, and kindness online. We empower students to believe in their capability, using technology with integrity and responsibility. Driven by curiosity and an aspirational mindset, students take a scholarly approach to computational thinking and problem-solving. By exploring how technology is created rather than merely consumed, students become innovative, skilled digital leaders ready for the future.
Key Stage 3
Computing is taught in one 55-minute lesson each week. Students explore fundamental computing concepts, develop coding skills and engage with a range of digital tools.
Key Stage 4
In KS4, Computing is taught in three 55-minute lessons per week in Year 10 and two in Year 11. Students deepen their understanding of advanced computing principles and prepare for formal assessments.

pageCache.pageTitle: English at the Charter School Bermondsey
pageCache.text:
English
Our English curriculum unlocks the power of language through diverse texts and critical thinking.
Curriculum Intent
English fosters an environment where students belong by sharing their voice with kindness and listening to others with respect. We inspire students to believe that literature transforms how we view the world, encouraging integrity in how they express truth and craft arguments. Driven by curiosity and an aspirational drive to break social barriers, students adopt a scholarly approach to reading, writing, and oracy. By exploring challenging texts beyond their comfort zone, students become articulate communicators capable of creating meaningful change.
Key Stage 3
Taught through 4.5 x 55-minute periods each week
At Key Stage 3, we focus on laying the foundation for high-level analysis and inference. Students explore a wide range of texts, including tragedies, from different cultures and time periods, ensuring exposure to diverse voices. Vocabulary development is a key priority, allowing students to articulate their own viewpoints and inferences. Reading is central to the curriculum, with students benefiting from weekly library lessons and participation in the accelerated reader programme.
Key Stage 4
Taught through 5 x 55-minute periods each week (6 for Year 11)
We follow the AQA specification, studying texts such as Macbeth, An Inspector Calls, A Christmas Carol, and the Power and Conflict Poetry anthology. Students also refine their descriptive and persuasive writing skills. Our goal is to provide them with the tools they need to pursue English studies at A Level and beyond.
Explore more
Health and Social Care BTEC
Personal Development

pageCache.pageTitle: Geography at the Charter School Bermondsey
pageCache.text:
Geography
Our Geography curriculum inspires curiosity and equips students to understand and navigate the complexities of our world
Curriculum Intent
Geography inspires fascination with our world, helping students belong by showing kindness and care for local and global communities. We build the belief that understanding environmental processes enables us to act with integrity for the planet’s future. Cultivating curiosity about natural and human environments, students apply a scholarly approach to data manipulation and landscape analysis. By exploring global challenges with high aspiration, students become knowledgeable geographers capable of solving complex world issues.
Key Stage 3
Taught through 2 x 55-minute periods each week
In Year 7, students engage with a concept-based curriculum designed to help them transition from Key Stage 2 while deepening their understanding of geographical skills and places. They will learn to describe trends, question, infer, interpret graphs, and explain using a geographical lens, with a focus on the United Kingdom to build local knowledge and understand the causes and consequences of wealth disparity and natural hazards.
In Years 8 and 9, students build upon the fundamental principles and skills from Year 7. The place-based curriculum allows them to apply their learning across various locations and recognise the links between place and theme. Students will analyse and interpret places and data, understand the connections between human and physical environments, and effectively communicate these concepts using geographical vocabulary. Complex themes such as climate change, coasts, and locations like Antarctica and Russia are explored, fostering a comprehensive understanding of the world and its key processes.
Key Stage 4
Taught through 3 x 55-minute periods each week
Students investigate the connections between physical and human themes on local and global scales. Following the AQA GCSE specification, they will explore case studies from the UK, higher-income countries (HICs), newly emerging economies (NEEs), and lower-income countries (LICs). Topics include climate change, poverty, deprivation, global shifts in economic power, and the challenge of sustainable resource use. Students are encouraged to understand their role in society by considering different viewpoints, values, and attitudes.
Explore more

pageCache.pageTitle: Health and Social Care BTEC at the Charter School Bermondsey
pageCache.text:
Health and Social Care BTEC
Gain the essential knowledge, practical skills, and compassionate mindset needed to kickstart a rewarding career in health and social care.
Curriculum Intent
Health and Social Care teaches students what it means to belong to a compassionate society, grounding learning in kindness, empathy, and professional integrity. Using real-life case studies, students believe in their ability to make a positive impact. Through curiosity about human development and a scholarly evaluation of health services, students set high aspirations for their future. By exploring career pathways in care, students become skilled, compassionate individuals ready to support others.
Key Stage 3
There is no KS3 Health and Social Care. Pupils may choose this BTEC as part of your KS4 curriculum.
Key Stage 4
Pupils will conplete a BTEC which is the equivalent of a GCSE. You are assessed through exams and coursework.

pageCache.pageTitle: History at the Charter School Bermondsey
pageCache.text:
History
Our History curriculum sparks curiosity and critical thinking, giving students the tools to understand past complexities and shape their futures.
Curriculum Intent
History helps students belong by recognising the diverse stories of those who came before us, fostering kindness and empathy across historical contexts. We instil the belief that evaluating evidence with integrity helps us understand the present. Sparking curiosity about past civilisations, students take a scholarly approach to source analysis and historical enquiry. By exploring historical periods with aspirational rigor, students become critical thinkers who learn from the past to shape a better future.
Key Stage 3
Taught through 2 x 55-minute periods each week
At KS3, students engage in historical enquiry, exploring primary and secondary sources. They study themes such as political institutions, belief systems, societal change, and human interconnectedness, building foundational skills for deeper historical understanding.
Key Stage 4
Taught through 3 x 55-minute periods each week
At KS4, students build on KS3 themes by studying topics like Life in Germany, Cold War tensions, Elizabeth I, and Health and the People. These topics encourage them to analyze societal developments and interconnected historical themes.
Explore more
Health and Social Care BTEC
Personal Development

pageCache.pageTitle: Maths at the Charter School Bermondsey
pageCache.text:
Maths
Our Maths curriculum builds strong foundations for critical thinking, problem-solving, and success in everyday life.
Curriculum Intent
Mathematics is a collaborative discipline where students belong by showing kindness, valuing different perspectives and supporting one another when problems become challenging. Grounded in the principles of mastery, we foster the belief that every problem can be approached and solved through integrity, resilience and systematic thinking. By nurturing curiosity and an aspirational mindset, students develop a scholarly approach to mathematical reasoning, justification and proof. Through exploring connections across mathematical concepts, students become confident, reflective problem-solvers, equipped for advanced study and life beyond the classroom.
Key Stage 3
Taught through 4.5 x 55-minute periods each week
Students explore the links between mathematical topics, connecting their learning from Key Stage 2 to Key Stage 4. We focus on developing fluency in mathematical concepts and structures, ensuring students can apply their knowledge to both routine and non-routine problems. This learning is enhanced with activities that encourage students to draw on previously mastered material, promoting problem-solving and mathematical reasoning.
Key Stage 4
Taught through 5 x 55-minute periods each week (6 for Year 11)
Students follow the Edexcel specification, building on their mathematical knowledge and skills to prepare for GCSEs and beyond. They engage with exam-style questions and develop techniques to succeed in their assessments. Our goal is to ensure every student reaches their full potential, regardless of background or prior learning, equipping them with the mathematical skills necessary for everyday life and further study.
Explore more
Health and Social Care BTEC
Personal Development

pageCache.pageTitle: Art at the Charter School Bermondsey
pageCache.text:
Art
Our Art and Design curriculum cultivates creativity and critical thinking, equipping you with essential skills to express your ideas.
Curriculum Intent
Art, craft, and design embody some of the highest forms of human creativity, showing students that "every child is an artist". Through studying Art and Design, students belong to an inclusive community built on kindness and integrity, where every form of expression is respected. We encourage students to believe in their artistic potential, fostering a curious mindset that embraces mistakes as opportunities for growth. By exploring diverse media, craft, and global cultures, students adopt a scholarly approach to practical techniques, raising their aspiration to become brave, expressive artists who communicate bold ideas.
Key Stage 3
Taught in one 55-minute lesson each week, KS3 Art projects are engaging and relevant, encouraging personal investigation and cultural exploration. In Year 7, students examine their local environment through a project on the Biscuit Factory. Year 8 links science and art, exploring the connection between word and image. In Year 9, students create symbolic sculptures and delve into identity through diverse artistic influences. Each project builds skills, confidence and visual literacy, enabling students to interpret and adapt artistic concepts in their own work.
Key Stage 4
In KS4, students follow the AQA Fine Art specification across three 55-minute lessons per week. They begin with skills-based mini-projects before embarking on sustained projects that encourage idea development from a range of sources. Students refine their work through experimentation with materials and techniques, building towards personal, meaningful responses. In Year 11, students complete an externally set assignment, selecting a starting point that meets the assessment criteria.
Explore more
Health and Social Care BTEC
Personal Development

pageCache.pageTitle: Design & Technology at the Charter School Bermondsey
pageCache.text:
Design & Technology
Master diverse techniques to innovate and design products that can shape the future.
Curriculum Intent
In GCSE Resistant Materials, students belong to a creative design studio where they collaborate safely, share workshop tools, and show kindness and integrity toward one another. We foster the belief that through curious exploration of woods, metals, polymers, and modern manufacturing processes, students can engineer real-world solutions to everyday challenges. Taking a scholarly approach to practical craftsmanship, iterative design, and testing, students build high aspirations to become resourceful, confident designers and skilled makers.
Key Stage 3
Taught in one to two 55-minute lessons each week, students study Food and Nutrition and Resistant Materials. They engage with set briefs, applying their skills and knowledge to innovate and create solutions. Reflection and evaluation are integral to the process, fostering a mindset of continuous improvement.
Key Stage 4
Design and Technology is taught in three 55-minute lessons each week in KS4.
We study Resistant Materials GCSE.

It is integrated into their experience of the curriculum as a whole and it is based on a partnership with the school, the students and their parents or carers. Our Careers Education programme promotes equality of opportunity, diversity and inclusion, whilst promoting the best interests of the students to whom it is given.

Our Team
A number of events, integrated into the school careers programme, offers a plethora of providers an opportunity to come into school to speak to pupils and/or their parents/carers. Students are also encouraged to attend the various career events that are planned throughout the year. Provider requiring access should contact our Careers Leader: Ms Jackson on ejackson@charterbermondsey.org.uk. 0203 542 6506
Our careers programme is reviewed every year, and the next review is in July 2027.
In order to facilitate provider access, the school will make the main hall, classrooms or private meeting rooms available for discussions between the provider and students, as appropriate to the activity. The school will also make available AV and other specialist equipment to support provider presentations. This will all be discussed and agreed in advance of the visit with Mr Haverty. Providers are welcome to leave a copy of their prospectus or other relevant course literature with Mr Haverty. This will be available for pupils to peruse in the school’s Library.
The school offers a comprehensive Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance programme.
Please speak to our Careers Advisor to identify the most suitable opportunity for you to engage with our students. Employers will be granted access in line with the school’s careers programme and calendar, with most opportunities available during National Careers Week, in March. Employers may be refused access if the provision does not meet an identified need in the School’s careers programme, or coincide with the calendar. Employers may also be refused access if they are unable to meet the school’s safeguarding policy.
Work Experience
Real-world experience is a vital part of our careers education.
Each year, our Year 10 students complete a week of work experience with an employer.
Students are given advice and support in school to prepare a CV and to contact employers to find a suitable placement. This helps them to learn about how to describe their skills and talents in a CV, and how to approach businesses and organisations when looking for work.
In recent years we have had students heading off to work in a wide range of interesting places from schools and hospitals, to film sets and engineering firms. Work experience is a valued part of our KS4 curriculum as it gives our young people the opportunity to find out more about the world of work and teaches them valuable skills such as communication, teamwork, timekeeping and organisation.

pageCache.pageTitle: Behaviour at The Charter School Bermondsey
pageCache.text:
Behaviour & Rewards
A calm, purposeful school where everyone can learn and thrive.
Belong
At Charter Bermondsey, we believe that great behaviour is the foundation of great learning. We have high expectations of every student, not because we are strict for its own sake, but because we know that a calm, respectful and orderly environment gives every pupil the best possible chance to succeed.
Our approach is built on mutual respect, clear expectations and genuine recognition of the effort students put in every day.
Our Approach
Our Expectations
We have high expectations of every student - in lessons, in communal spaces and in the way they treat the people around them. Arriving on time, coming prepared and showing respect for staff and peers are the baseline. Our Parent Handbook sets out everything families need to know.
Rewards
We recognise effort and achievement loudly and often. Students earn recognition for excellent work, positive attitude, strong attendance and contributions to school life. Achievements are celebrated through Learning Family Time, postcards and calls home, termly rewards events and our student leadership programme.
Attendance
We expect every student to be in school every day, on time and ready to learn. Our target is 96% attendance or above. We work closely with families where attendance is a concern before taking any formal action.
